findings.title: BonusScale clamp is not enforced when BonusPrefix is raised afterwards; Match() exceeds 1
findings.property: after any sequence of BonusScale/BonusPrefix calls, Match() stays within 0..1 (scale never exceeds 1/BonusPrefix)
findings.evidence: Doc: 'To guarantee that the similarity score remains in the interval 0..1, this scaling factor is not allowed to exceed 1 / BonusPrefix.' The clamp is only applied inside BonusScale, so a later BonusPrefix(v) (which does not re-clamp) breaks the invariant; Similarity range 0..1 is promised for Match.

propertyCheck.example: Failing test case: sc: 1, pr: 50, s1: "aaaaa", s2: "aaaaaa"

review.title: Match() can return a score above 1 when BonusPrefix is raised after BonusScale
review.reason: The BonusScale doc says the scale is "not allowed to exceed 1 / BonusPrefix" so that the score stays within 0..1. The clamp runs only inside BonusScale (params.go:136), and BonusPrefix (params.go:118) sets the value without re-checking. So `BonusScale(0.25).BonusPrefix(10)` gives prefix*scale = 2.5. Match then computes sim + pl*scale*(1-sim) = 0.95 + 10*0.25*0.05 = 1.075, which is real arithmetic and not a float artefact. The same state can also make the `1 - bonusPrefix*bonusScale` divisor in the minScore pre-computation (levenshtein.go:268) zero or negative. A maintainer would likely fix this by re-clamping in BonusPrefix or clamping at use time in Match.

findings.title: Calculate with maxCost returns a within-budget distance that is far below the true distance
findings.property: with maxCost>0, the result equals the exact distance if that is <= maxCost, otherwise it is a value > maxCost (a lower bound of the true distance)
findings.input: Calculate("aaa", "bbbab", maxCost=2, insCost=1, subCost=2, delCost=2); also Similarity("aaa","bbbab", InsCost(1).SubCost(2).DelCost(2).MinScore(0.75))
findings.expected: true distance is 6 > maxCost, so Calculate returns a value > 2 (e.g. 3); Similarity with MinScore 0.75 returns 0 (true score 0.25)
findings.actual: Calculate returns 2 (looks like an exact in-budget distance); Similarity with MinScore 0.75 returns 0.75 instead of 0 (without MinScore it returns 0.25)
findings.evidence: Docstring: 'If maxCost is non-zero, the calculation stops as soon as the distance is determined to be greater than maxCost. Therefore, any return value higher than maxCost is a lower bound for the actual distance.' Implied: a value <= maxCost is exact. Similarity/Match docs: scores lower than MinScore are returned as 0; here a 0.25 score is reported as 0.75.

error.message: Calculate with maxCost=2 returned 2, but actual distance is 6 (> maxCost)

review.title: Calculate with maxCost>0 returns an in-budget distance (2) when the true distance is 6
review.reason: The input is valid (non-negative costs, maxCost=2). By my hand calculation the true distance for "aaa"→"bbbab" with ins=1, sub=2, del=2 is 6: two substitutions, one match and two insertions. The docs promise that only values above maxCost may be lower bounds, so a value ≤ maxCost should be exact. The repro failed when I ran it, and Calculate returned 2, which looks like an exact in-budget distance. That makes Similarity with MinScore=0.75 return 0.75 instead of 0 (the true score is 0.25). The cause is probably the banded pruning in the maxCost path, which runs after the string swap, so the cost asymmetry (ins≠del) is involved. I did not trace the exact line. A maintainer would fix this because it silently gives wrong results.

findings.title: Similarity/Match return NaN when the maximum possible distance is 0 due to zero costs
findings.property: Similarity and Match always return a score in 0..1 for valid (non-negative) costs
findings.input: Similarity("", "a", NewParams().InsCost(0)) and Match with the same params
findings.actual: NaN (0/0, since maxDist is 0 and dist is 0)
findings.evidence: Docs: 'The score is in the range of 0..1'; costs 'must be zero or positive' so 0 is explicitly allowed; the code comment shows the author intends to avoid divByZero issues but only guards the both-empty case.

error.message: score for "" vs "a" with InsCost(0) = NaN, want within 0..1

review.title: Similarity/Match return NaN when maxDist is 0 because of zero edit costs
review.reason: InsCost(0) is documented as valid ("must be zero or positive"), and Match is documented to return a score in 0..1. For ("", "a") with InsCost(0), l1=0 and l2=1, so maxDist = 0*delCost + 1*0 = 0 and dist = 0. Line 276 then computes 1 - 0/0, which is NaN. The only guard is the both-empty shortcut at line 230, and its comment says it exists to avoid divide-by-zero. The same case can arise with other zero-cost configurations. A maintainer would likely accept a small fix that returns 1, or a defined value, when maxDist == 0.
